subject: maths
title: Nets of Objects: Cubes, Prisms, Pyramids, Cylinders and Cones
seo_title: Year 5 Nets Worksheets: Nets of Cubes, Prisms, Pyramids, Cylinders and Cones (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Connect objects to their nets and build objects from their nets using spatial and geometric reasoning
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on nets for the Australian Curriculum: match objects to their nets, count faces, edges and vertices, find which patterns fold into a cube, work out opposite faces and edges that meet, and solve box, tent and party hat problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: A net is a flat shape that folds into an object: each part of the net becomes one face.
key_sub: Count the shapes to name the object: 6 squares make a cube, 2 triangles and 3 rectangles make a triangular prism, 2 circles and a rectangle make a cylinder. In a cube net, squares in a line with one square between them become opposite faces.
body_html:
What is a net?

A net is a flat shape that folds up to make an object. Each part of the net becomes one face. Look at the shapes in the net and count them to name the object.

ObjectShapes in the netFacesEdgesVertices
Cube6 equal squares6128
Rectangular prism6 rectangles (3 matching pairs)6128
Triangular prism2 triangles, 3 rectangles596
Square-based pyramid1 square, 4 triangles585
Triangular pyramid4 triangles464
Cylinder2 circles, 1 rectangle2 flat faces, 1 curved surface––
Cone1 circle, 1 fan shape1 flat face, 1 curved surface––

A prism has the same shape at both ends, joined by rectangles. A pyramid has one base and triangles that meet at a point.

Example 1

A net has 1 square and 4 triangles. Which object does it make?

The square is the base. The 4 triangles fold up and meet at a point.

Answer: a square-based pyramid

Nets of a cube

A cube has 11 different nets. A pattern of 6 squares is not a net if two squares fold onto the same face.

Patterns that are never nets of a cube: 5 squares in a row, a 2-by-2 block of squares, and two squares on the same side of a row of 4.

Fold it in your head

Squares in a straight line with one square between them become opposite faces. Squares that touch in the net always touch on the cube.

Example 2

This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?

A, B and C are in a straight line, with B between A and C. So A and C are opposite.

Answer: face C

Example 3

Which face is opposite face E?

E, B and F are in a straight line (going down), with B between them.

Answer: face F

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking any 6 squares make a cubeFold each square in your head. No row of 5, no 2-by-2 block, no two squares on the same side of a row of 4
Counting only the faces you can seeCount the hidden faces too: a rectangular prism always has 6 faces
Mixing up prisms and pyramidsA prism has 2 matching ends and rectangles; a pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point
Mixing up a cylinder and a coneA cylinder’s net has 2 circles and a rectangle; a cone’s has 1 circle and a fan shape
Saying faces that touch in the net are oppositeFaces that touch in the net are next to each other on the object
Swapping edges and verticesEdges are the lines where faces meet; vertices are the corners

faq.q: What do Year 5 students learn about nets in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 5 (AC9M5SP01) students connect objects to their nets and build objects from nets, using spatial reasoning to see how a flat net folds into a cube, prism, pyramid, cylinder or cone.

faq.q: How many nets does a cube have?
faq.a: A cube has 11 different nets. Each one has 6 squares, and no two squares fold onto the same face.

faq.q: How can you tell if a net will fold into a cube?
faq.a: It needs 6 squares that cover 6 different faces. A row of 5 squares, a 2-by-2 block, or two squares on the same side of a row of 4 will never fold into a cube.

faq.q: Are nets in the Year 5 NAPLAN numeracy test?
faq.a: They can be. NAPLAN numeracy includes questions on space, such as matching objects to their nets or counting faces, edges and vertices.

sets.title: Name the object from its net

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There is 1 square (the base) and 4 triangles that meet at a point. They fold into a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There are 2 circles (the flat ends) and a rectangle that rolls up into the curved surface. They fold into a cylinder. The circles can touch the rectangle anywhere along its long edges.

items.q: A net has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. Which object does it make?
items.e: The 2 triangles are the ends and the 3 rectangles join them, so it is a triangular prism. A pyramid has triangles that meet at a point, not rectangles.
There is 1 circle (the base) and a fan shape (part of a circle) that rolls up into the curved surface with a point. They fold into a cone.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 2 circles (the flat ends) and a rectangle that rolls up into the curved surface. They fold into a cylinder.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. They fold into a rectangular prism.
There is 1 circle (the base) and a fan shape (part of a circle) that rolls up into the curved surface with a point. They fold into a cone.

items.q: A net has 1 square and 4 triangles. Which object does it make?
items.e: The square is the base and the 4 triangles meet at a point at the top, so it is a square-based pyramid. A pyramid is named after the shape of its base.

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. They fold into a rectangular prism. The top and bottom are squares, but the 4 sides are thin rectangles, so it is not a cube.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. One is the base and the other 3 meet at a point, so they fold into a triangular pyramid.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles joining them. They fold into a triangular prism.

items.q: A net has 1 circle and 1 fan shape (part of a circle). Which object does it make?
items.e: The fan shape rolls up into a curved surface that comes to a point, and the circle is the base, so it makes a cone.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. They fold into a rectangular prism. Two faces are squares, but the other 4 are long rectangles, so it is not a cube.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles joining them. They fold into a triangular prism. The triangles do not have to be equilateral.

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: D has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. The others make a square-based pyramid and a triangular pyramid, and one has only 2 rectangles, so it cannot close up.

items.q: A net has 4 triangles and no other shapes. Which object does it make?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. One is the base and the other 3 meet at a point, so they fold into a triangular pyramid.

items.q: Which net folds into a closed cylinder?
items.e: B has a rectangle with a circle on each long edge: one on the top and one on the bottom. One wrong net has only 1 circle, one has both circles at the same end, and one is the net of a cone.

items.q: A net has 2 circles and 1 rectangle. Which object does it make?
items.e: The rectangle rolls into a tube and the 2 circles close the ends, so it makes a cylinder. A cone has only 1 circle.

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There are 6 squares, all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 6 squares, all the same size. They fold into a cube.

sets.title: Faces, edges and vertices of objects

items.q: Which object has 9 edges and 6 vertices?
items.e: A triangular prism has 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 on each triangle end).

items.q: This net is folded into an object. How many vertices will the object have?
items.e: The net folds into a triangular prism. Each triangle end has 3 corners: 3 + 3 = 6 vertices. 5 is the number of faces in the net.

items.q: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. There are 3 corners on each triangle end: 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. You can see only 3 faces. The bottom, the back and one side are hidden, but they still count.

items.q: How many vertices does a hexagonal prism have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons and 6 rectangles), 18 edges and 12 vertices. 6 corners on each hexagon end: 6 + 6 = 12.
A cone has 1 flat circle face (the base) and 1 curved surface that comes to a point. Its net is a circle and a fan shape.

items.q: This is a pentagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons and 5 rectangles), 15 edges and 10 vertices. 2 pentagon ends + 5 rectangles = 7.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Vertices are the corners: 4 at the front and 4 at the back.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. 4 edges round the base and 4 going up to the top: 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. 4 corners on the base and 1 at the top: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: Which object has 5 faces and 5 vertices?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square, 4 triangles) and 5 vertices (4 on the base, 1 at the top). A triangular prism also has 5 faces, but it has 6 vertices.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. 3 edges round each triangle end and 3 long edges joining them: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

items.q: How many edges does a triangular pyramid have?
items.e: A triangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. 3 edges round the base and 3 going up to the top: 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: This is a triangular pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Do not forget the triangle base underneath.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Do not forget the square base underneath.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Dashed lines show the edges at the back that you cannot see.
A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces, one at each end, and 1 curved surface round the side.

items.q: A pyramid has a hexagon for its base. How many faces does it have?
items.e: The base is 1 hexagon, and there is 1 triangle on each of its 6 sides: 1 + 6 = 7 faces. 8 is the number of faces of a hexagonal prism (2 hexagons and 6 rectangles).

items.q: How many edges does a rectangular prism have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. There are 4 edges on the top, 4 on the bottom and 4 going up the sides.

items.q: This net is folded into an object. How many edges will the object have?
items.e: It folds into a square-based pyramid: 4 edges round the square base and 4 edges going up to the top: 4 + 4 = 8.

sets.title: Which nets fold into a cube?

items.q: These 5 squares are part of a net of a cube. Where should the 6th square go?
items.e: With the square at A, the 6 squares fold onto 6 different faces. At each of the other places, two squares would fold onto the same face and one face would be left open.

items.q: These 5 squares are part of a net of a cube. Where should the 6th square go?
items.e: With the square at A, the 6 squares fold onto 6 different faces. At each of the other places, two squares would fold onto the same face and one face would be left open.

items.q: How many different nets does a cube have? (A net that is only turned or flipped over counts as the same net.)
items.e: A cube has 11 different nets. 6 is the number of faces, 12 the number of edges and 8 the number of vertices.

items.e: No: it has a 2-by-2 block of squares, but only 3 faces of a cube meet at a corner, so two squares overlap. A cube has 6 faces, so 6 squares is the right number, but they must be in the right places.

items.e: No: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way round, so the first and last squares land on the same face. A cube has 6 faces, so 6 squares is the right number, but they must be in the right places.

sets.title: Fold it in your head: opposite faces, corners and edges

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which blue edge is taped to the red edge?
items.e: When the net is folded, the red edge and edge D end up on the same edge of the cube, so they are taped together. Fold one square at a time and follow where the red edge goes.

items.q: This net is folded into a square-based pyramid. Where do the points of the 4 triangles meet?
c: in the middle of the square
at the 4 corners of the square
items.e: Fold each triangle up from the square. Their points all meet at 1 vertex at the top, above the middle of the square.

items.q: This is a net of a dice. The numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. What number goes on the face marked ?
items.e: When the net is folded, the face marked ? is opposite the 6. So the missing number is 7 − 6 = 1.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube with face C on the bottom. Which face is on the top?
items.e: Fold the net: face F lands opposite face C. A face that touches C in the net (A, D) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which 3 faces meet at the corner with the red dot?
items.e: Every corner of a cube is where 3 faces meet. In the net the dot touches F; when you fold the net, D and E fold up to the same corner, so the 3 faces are D, E and F.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face D?
items.e: Faces D and C are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which blue edge is taped to the red edge?
items.e: When the net is folded, the red edge and edge B end up on the same edge of the cube, so they are taped together. Fold one square at a time and follow where the red edge goes.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which blue edge is taped to the red edge?
items.e: When the net is folded, the red edge and edge C end up on the same edge of the cube, so they are taped together. Fold one square at a time and follow where the red edge goes.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which blue edge is taped to the red edge?
items.e: When the net is folded, the red edge and edge B end up on the same edge of the cube, so they are taped together. Fold one square at a time and follow where the red edge goes.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube with face B on the bottom. Which face is on the top?
items.e: Faces B and D are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: In the net, face F touches only 1 other face. When the net is folded into a cube, how many faces will touch face F?
items.e: On a cube, every face touches 4 other faces. Only the opposite face (face B) does not touch it.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which blue edge is taped to the red edge?
items.e: When the net is folded, the red edge and edge A end up on the same edge of the cube, so they are taped together. Fold one square at a time and follow where the red edge goes.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which 3 faces meet at the corner with the red dot?
items.e: Every corner of a cube is where 3 faces meet. In the net the dot touches E and F; when you fold the net, D folds up to the same corner, so the 3 faces are D, E and F.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which 3 faces meet at the corner with the red dot?
items.e: Every corner of a cube is where 3 faces meet. In the net the dot touches C and E; when you fold the net, D folds up to the same corner, so the 3 faces are C, D and E.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which 3 faces meet at the corner with the red dot?
items.e: Every corner of a cube is where 3 faces meet. In the net the dot touches B; when you fold the net, A and E fold up to the same corner, so the 3 faces are A, B and E.

items.q: This net is folded into a rectangular prism. Which face is opposite face Q?
items.e: Faces Q and S are the same size and have one face (R) between them in the strip, so they fold onto opposite sides. In a rectangular prism, opposite faces are always the same size and shape.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face does NOT touch face B?
items.e: Fold the net: face F lands opposite face B. A face that touches B in the net (A) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face C?
items.e: Fold the net: face B lands opposite face C. A face that touches C in the net (F) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This is a net of a dice. The numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. What number goes on the face marked ?
items.e: When the net is folded, the face marked ? is opposite the 3. So the missing number is 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which blue edge is taped to the red edge?
items.e: When the net is folded, the red edge and edge D end up on the same edge of the cube, so they are taped together. Fold one square at a time and follow where the red edge goes.

sets.title: Nets in real life: boxes, tents, cans and party hats

items.q: A party hat is shaped like a cone with no base. What shape is its net?
c: a fan shape (part of a circle)
items.e: A cone’s curved surface is made from a fan shape. With no base, the hat needs only that one piece. A triangle has straight edges, so it cannot roll into a round cone.

items.q: Kai cuts out a net of a cube (6 squares in one piece) and folds it. How many edges must he tape to close the cube?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges. The 6 squares of the net are joined by 5 folds, so 12 − 5 = 7 edges are still open and need tape.

items.q: A play tent has the shape of a triangular prism, but it has no floor. How many faces of fabric does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces. Without the floor there are 5 − 1 = 4: 2 triangle ends and 2 sloping sides.

items.q: A cereal box is a rectangular prism. It is 20 cm wide, 30 cm tall and 6 cm deep. How many faces of the box measure 20 cm by 30 cm?
items.e: The front and the back are both 20 cm by 30 cm. Opposite faces of a rectangular prism are the same size.

items.q: Isla makes a model of a square-based pyramid with straws and connectors: one straw for each edge and one connector for each vertex. What does she need?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 8 edges (4 round the base and 4 up to the top) and 5 vertices (4 on the base and 1 at the top).

items.q: A camping tent is a triangular prism with a floor. How many pieces of fabric are needed if each face is one piece?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangles (2 sloping sides and the floor).

items.q: A tube for tennis balls is a cylinder with a lid and a base. Which shapes are in its net?
items.e: The curved side unrolls into 1 rectangle, and the lid and base are 2 circles.

items.q: Chloe paints each face of a shoe box (a rectangular prism with a lid) a different colour. How many colours does she use?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, so she needs 6 colours. 12 is the number of edges and 8 the number of vertices.

items.q: The frame of a play tent has a pole along every edge of a triangular prism. How many poles are there?
items.e: A triangular prism has 9 edges: 3 round each triangle end and 3 long edges joining them.

items.q: Jack glues 2 cubes together, face to face, to make a rectangular prism. How many faces does the new object have?
items.e: The new object is a rectangular prism, and every rectangular prism has 6 faces. The two faces that are glued together are hidden inside.

items.q: Mei makes an open box (a cube with no lid) to hold pencils. How many squares are in the net?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, but there is no lid, so the net has 6 − 1 = 5 squares.

items.q: The ends of a triangular chocolate box are triangles with all 3 sides 4 cm. The box is 20 cm long. What size is each rectangle in the net?
items.e: Each rectangle is as wide as one side of the triangle (4 cm) and as long as the box (20 cm), so it is 4 cm by 20 cm.

items.q: A model cube is made with straws, one straw for each edge. Each straw is 10 cm long. What is the total length of the straws?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges: 12 × 10 = 120 cm. 60 cm counts the faces (6) and 80 cm counts the vertices (8).

items.q: Mia makes a model cone with a base. Which shapes does she cut out?
c: a fan shape and a circle
items.e: The fan shape rolls into the curved surface and the circle is the base. A rectangle and 2 circles make a cylinder.

items.q: A net of a square-based pyramid (a square with a triangle on each side) is folded up. How many edges need tape?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 8 edges. The 4 triangles are joined to the square by 4 folds, so 8 − 4 = 4 edges need tape.

items.q: Sienna makes a gift box shaped like a rectangular prism, with a lid. How many rectangles does she need in the net?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces: top (the lid), bottom and 4 sides. 8 is the number of vertices.

items.q: A chocolate bar comes in a long box shaped like a triangular prism. Which shapes are in the net of the box?
items.e: The 2 triangles are the ends of the box and the 3 rectangles are its long sides.

items.q: The label of a cylinder-shaped can goes all the way round once, with no overlap. How long is the label?
c: the distance round the top of the can
twice the height of the can
the width across the top of the can
items.e: The long edge of the rectangle wraps round the circle once, so it is as long as the distance round the circle. The short edge of the label is the height of the can.

items.q: Cooper makes a net of a cube from card. Each square is 10 cm by 10 cm. How much card is in the net?
items.e: Each square has an area of 10 × 10 = 100 cm². There are 6 squares: 6 × 100 = 600 cm². 400 cm² counts only 4 faces.

items.q: A can of tomatoes is a cylinder. The paper label goes all the way round the can once, with no overlap. What shape is the label when it is peeled off and laid flat?
items.e: The curved surface of a cylinder unrolls into a rectangle. The 2 circles are the top and bottom of the can.
